SMTO-EXE-0119 — SMTO can't find the file to upload on the Gateway computer

GUID: af32533d-04d4-5f49-872b-555222e4b7a0
Slug: browser-file-not-found-on-target
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • To upload a file, the file must be on the computer where SMTO's browser runs, and SMTO couldn't find or read it there. Nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Tell SMTO the full location of the file on the Gateway computer, such as /home/alex/Documents/report.pdf or C:\Users\alex\Documents\report.pdf. SMTO needs the complete location; a file name alone isn't enough.
  2. If the file is on another computer, ask SMTO to copy it to this Gateway first, then upload the copy. SMTO's browser can only upload files stored on its own computer.
  3. Make sure it is a normal file, not a folder or a shortcut, and that the Gateway's user account is allowed to open it. SMTO refuses folders, shortcuts and files it has no permission to read.
  4. Don't use a shared network location, such as one starting with two slashes. Copy the file onto the Gateway computer instead. Network share locations are refused for uploads.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the file was attached, and the website shows the file name in its upload field.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's location, to the person who manages the Gateway. Files larger than 16 MB can't be uploaded through SMTO's browser.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The browser upload source path on the selected Gateway is not absolute, not a regular file, contains '..' or a network-share prefix, or could not be read (OS error).

What this means

  • Upload preparation rejected a nonabsolute, missing, nonregular or unsafe target-local path, or reading the file raised an OS error. The file need not be literally absent in every case. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Upload preparation rejected a nonabsolute, missing, nonregular or unsafe target-local path, or reading the file raised an OS error. The file need not be literally absent in every case.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact Gateway-local path, file type, link/path restrictions and access under the Gateway account.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend.execute rejects upload_file paths that are relative, not is_file(), contain '..', or start with // or \, and maps any OSError from the no-follow regular-file read to file_not_found_on_target. Supply an absolute regular-file path on the selected Gateway that the Gateway's OS account can read (16 MiB maximum); transfer the file from another Gateway with gateway.copy first.
  • Use an accessible supported absolute regular-file path on the selected Gateway; transfer from another machine through the supported copy flow when necessary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an absolute regular-file path on the selected Gateway. Use gateway.copy first if the source is on another Gateway.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended bounded regular file is read successfully on the selected Gateway before upload.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
